books.section: Christian Fundamentalism and the Religious Right
The 'Moral Majority' and Focus on the Family

primary_sources: Photograph by David E. Lucas, 'I Love America' rally, Ohio Statehouse, September 17, 1979 (Columbus Metropolitan Library via DPLA)

source: original; stimulus photograph viewed before writing

stimulus.source_note: Photograph: Reverend Jerry Falwell at an 'I Love America' rally, Ohio Statehouse, Columbus, Ohio, September 17, 1979, by David E. Lucas (Columbus Metropolitan Library, via DPLA/Wikimedia Commons), public domain. Account drawn from the grounding books (Barron's Ch. 10, Topic 8.14; 5 Steps Ch. 28; Princeton Ch. 12).
stimulus.text: The photograph shows the Reverend Jerry Falwell speaking into a microphone on the steps of the Ohio Statehouse in Columbus, Ohio, on September 17, 1979, at an 'I Love America' rally. Behind him stands a choir of young men in white suits and young women in long red dresses with their heads bowed, and six American flags stand before the building's stone columns.

stem: What does the photograph best show about Falwell's rallies?

options.text: They were private church services with no public message at all.
options.misconception: The rally is on the steps of a state capitol, with a speaker, flags, and a crowd, so it is public.

options.text: They opposed every public display of religion in American life.
options.misconception: The photograph shows a public religious rally, the opposite of opposing public religion.

options.text: They mixed religion and patriotism, with prayer and flags on capitol steps.
They were concerts with no speaker and no political message.
options.misconception: Falwell stands at a microphone in the center, speaking, so the rally had a speaker.

rationales.A: The rally is on the steps of a state capitol, with a speaker, flags, and a crowd, so it is public.
rationales.B: The photograph shows a public religious rally, the opposite of opposing public religion.
rationales.C: The choir stands with bowed heads behind Falwell, six flags stand before the columns, and the rally fills the capitol steps.
rationales.D: Falwell stands at a microphone in the center, speaking, so the rally had a speaker.
rationales.general:
1. Look at what the camera shows: a preacher at a microphone on capitol steps.
2. Behind him a choir stands with bowed heads, and six American flags stand before the columns.
3. Prayer, flags, and a state capitol together mix religion with patriotism in public.
Remember: In a photograph, the setting is evidence too, so read the flags and the building.
